title: Grandma’s 25-Minute Fluffy Buttermilk Biscuits (Under $3 a Batch!)
description: Skip the pricey brunch takeout! These fluffy buttermilk biscuits bake up golden and sky-high in 25 minutes using budget-friendly pantry staples.
story: Last Sunday, I almost caved and ordered a weekend biscuit sandwich pack from our local bakery down the street. It would’ve set me back $24 after delivery fees and tip! Instead, I pulled out a $2 bag of Aldi all-purpose flour and half a block of butter from my cramped apartment fridge to see what I could pull off. Honestly, Grandma knew what she was doing keeping this recipe under half an hour. The first time I tested making these on my own, I made the rookie mistake of twisting my biscuit cutter back and forth, which pinched the dough together and gave me sad, flat hockey pucks. Once I learned to press straight down and fold the dough like an envelope, they puffed into the tallest, flaky layers imaginable. The whole batch cost about $2.40 to whip up, and eating them warm with a swipe of salted butter totally saved my Sunday budget.
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour (spooned and leveled, plus extra for dusting)
8 tablespoons (1 stick) cold unsalted butter (frozen for 15 minutes)
3/4 cup cold whole buttermilk (plus 1 tablespoon for brushing tops)
1 tablespoon melted salted butter (for brushing warm biscuits)
instructions: Step 1: Preheat your oven to 450°F and line a small baking sheet with parchment paper. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and kosher salt until evenly distributed.

Step 2: Take your cold butter from the freezer and grate it directly into the flour mixture using the large holes of a box grater. Gently toss the butter shreds with your fingers until coated and crumbly—work fast so the butter doesn't warm up.

Step 3: Pour in the cold buttermilk and stir with a fork just until a shaggy dough forms. Turn the dough onto a lightly floured counter and gently pat it into a rectangle. Fold it in half like a book, turn it 90 degrees, and repeat 3 to 4 times to build distinct flaky layers.

Step 4: Pat the dough down to about 3/4-inch thickness. Cut out biscuits using a sharp 2.5-inch round cutter, pressing straight down without twisting. Arrange biscuits touching each other on the sheet, brush tops lightly with buttermilk, and bake for 13 to 15 minutes until deep golden brown and fragrant. Brush with melted butter right out of the oven.
proHack: Pop your wrapped stick of butter in the freezer for 15 minutes before starting, then grate it straight into the dry bowl. The tiny shreds disperse instantly without you overworking the dough, keeping the butter cold enough to explode into steam and create massive rise in the oven.
storage: Keep leftover biscuits in an airtight container or zip-top bag at room temperature for up to 3 days, or freeze them wrapped tightly in foil for 2 months. Reheat in a 350°F toaster oven for 5 minutes to get the crisp, buttery bottoms back without turning them rubbery.

faqs.question: Can I substitute regular milk if I don't have buttermilk?
faqs.answer: Yes! Just pour 1 tablespoon of fresh lemon juice or white vinegar into a measuring cup, then fill it to the 3/4 cup mark with whole milk. Let it sit on the counter for 5 minutes until lightly curdled, or swap in 3/4 cup of plain Greek yogurt thinned out with a splash of milk.

faqs.question: How do I prevent my biscuits from baking flat and dense?
faqs.answer: Never twist your biscuit cutter! Twisting pinches the layered dough edges shut and prevents the steam from pushing the biscuit upward. Press straight down, pull straight up, and tuck the raw biscuits closely against each other on the pan so they support each other as they climb.
